import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Load the dataset from the provided string
data = """amount,is_fraud,transaction_type,hour_of_day
115.02,0,refund,22
44.37,0,payment,5
144.25,0,transfer,21
536.22,0,payment,17
38.43,0,payment,5
"""
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Convert 'is_fraud' to a categorical type for clearer labels in the plots
# '0' will be labeled 'Not Fraud' and '1' as 'Fraud'
df['is_fraud'] = df['is_fraud'].astype(str).replace({'0': 'Not Fraud', '1': 'Fraud'})

# Set a consistent theme for the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure with two subplots arranged vertically
# This allows for showing different aspects of the data side-by-side
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(12, 10))
fig.suptitle('Transaction Analysis by Hour, Type, and Amount', fontsize=16)

# --- Plot 1: Transaction Count by Hour of Day and Fraud Status ---
# This plot helps identify if certain hours have a higher volume of fraudulent transactions.
# With the provided sample data, all 'is_fraud' values are 'Not Fraud', so only one hue category will be visible.
sns.countplot(data=df, x='hour_of_day', hue='is_fraud', ax=axes[0], palette='viridis')
axes[0].set_title('Transaction Count by Hour of Day and Fraud Status', fontsize=14)
axes[0].set_xlabel('Hour of Day', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_ylabel('Number of Transactions', fontsize=12)
axes[0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45) # Rotate x-axis labels for better readability if many hours
axes[0].legend(title='Fraud Status', loc='upper right')
axes[0].set_xticks(range(24)) # Ensure all 24 hours are represented if data was denser

# --- Plot 2: Transaction Amount Distribution by Transaction Type and Fraud Status ---
# This plot helps visualize if fraudulent transactions tend to have different amounts
# compared to non-fraudulent ones, and how this varies across transaction types.
# For the given sample data:
# - 'refund' and 'transfer' will show single lines as there's only one transaction of each type.
# - 'payment' will show a proper box plot as there are three transactions of this type.
# - Again, only 'Not Fraud' will be visible due to the sample data.
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='transaction_type', y='amount', hue='is_fraud', ax=axes[1], palette='plasma')
axes[1].set_title('Transaction Amount Distribution by Transaction Type and Fraud Status', fontsize=14)
axes[1].set_xlabel('Transaction Type', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_ylabel('Transaction Amount', fontsize=12)
axes[1].legend(title='Fraud Status', loc='upper right')

# Adjust layout to prevent titles/labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.95])

# Save the generated visualization as 'output.png'
plt.savefig('output.png')
